issues.legal_issue: Omitting some legal representatives of a deceased appellant from the record does not necessarily cause the pending appeal to abate when the representatives on record represent the estate and no circumstance makes the proceeding unfair to the absent heirs.
material_facts: A plaintiff-appellant died while an appeal was pending, and his widow and major son were substituted as his heirs within time.
Three other heirs were not brought on record; the objection that the appeal had abated was raised only in the further appeal.
The court found no fraud or collusion, no indication that the trial had been unfair or unreal, and no special case against an absent heir that could not have been tried in the proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The estate was sufficiently represented by the heirs on record, who represented the absent heirs and whose result would bind them. The appeal had not abated; the judgment finding abatement was set aside and the case remanded for a decision on the merits after the omitted heirs were brought on record.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXII Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, omission to bring every heir of a deceased plaintiff or appellant on record does not by itself cause abatement. The heirs brought on record may represent the entire estate, and the absent heirs may be bound, unless fraud or collusion, circumstances showing that there was no fair or real trial, or a special defence of an absent heir that could not be tried in the proceeding is shown. The Court applied Daya Ram v. Shyam Sundari and N. K. Mohd. Sulaiman Sahib v. N. C. Mohd. Ismail Saheb, and approved the approach in the other cited cases.

rule.if: appeal_pending and appellant_died and some_heirs_substituted and other_heirs_omitted and omission_not_deliberate and estate_represented_by_substituted_heirs and not fraud_or_collusion and not unfair_or_unreal_trial and not untried_special_defence

predicates.appeal_pending: An appeal against a decree was pending when a party to it died.
predicates.appellant_died: A party who was an appellant in the pending appeal died.
predicates.some_heirs_substituted: One or more heirs of the deceased appellant were brought on record in the appeal.
predicates.other_heirs_omitted: One or more other heirs of the deceased appellant were not brought on record.
predicates.omission_not_deliberate: The omission of the other heirs was not a deliberate exclusion.
predicates.estate_represented_by_substituted_heirs: The heirs brought on record represented the deceased person's estate, including the interests of the omitted heirs.
predicates.fraud_or_collusion: There was fraud or collusion in the representation of the estate in the proceeding.
predicates.unfair_or_unreal_trial: Circumstances showed that the proceeding did not provide a fair or real trial.
predicates.untried_special_defence: An omitted heir had a special defence that was not and could not be tried in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal is pending at an appellant's death, some heirs are substituted and others are omitted, the appeal does not abate if the omission was not deliberate, the substituted heirs represent the estate, and there was no fraud or collusion, unfair or unreal trial, or untried special defence.
